title: Let him come with us
goal: Plan a Saturday trip with Sēf and say who should come along and who drives
tip: khalli 'let' takes the person as an ending, and the verb after it agrees: khallah yrūḥ 'let him go', khallhum yiyūn 'let them come'. To a woman add -ī-: khallīh yrūḥ. Before a name you'll hear khalli or khall: khalli Fahad ysūg 'let Fahad drive'.
grammar: khalli + object ending + present verb: 'let him / them do'
dialogue: A
يوم السبت بنروح رأس الخيمة. تبي تيي ويانا؟
yōm is-sabt binrūḥ Rās il-Khēma. tabi tiyi wiyyāna?
We're going to Ras Al Khaimah on Saturday. Do you want to come with us?
B
أكيد! وفهد؟ خله يروح ويانا بعد
akīd! w Fahad? khallah yrūḥ wiyyāna baʿad
Definitely! What about Fahad? Let him come with us too.
A
زين، بس سيارتي ما فيها مكان
zēn, bas sayyārti ma fīha makān
Fine, but there's no room in my car.
B
عادي، خله يسوق سيارته. يحب السواقة وايد
ʿādi, khallah ysūg sayyārtah. yḥibb is-swāga wāyid
No problem, let him drive his car. He loves driving.
A
صح. وعيال عمي يبون ييون بعد
ṣaḥḥ. w ʿyāl ʿammi yabūn yiyūn baʿad
True. And my cousins want to come too.
B
خلهم ييون! أحسن، نروح كلنا ويا بعض
khallhum yiyūn! aḥsan, nrūḥ killna wiyya baʿaẓ
Let them come! Even better, we'll all go together.
A
زين. بس خلي فهد يعرف: لازم ما يتأخر!
zēn. bas khalli Fahad yaʿarf: lāzim ma yitʼakhkhar!
OK. But make sure Fahad knows he mustn't be late!
B
ماشي، بقول له. يلا، نشوفك السبت
māshi, bagūl-lah. yalla, nshūfak is-sabt
OK, I'll tell him. Right, see you on Saturday.
items: let him go, let him come along (to a man)
to a woman: khallīh yrūḥ (خليه يروح); khallah yrūḥ wiyyāna = let him come with us
to a woman: khallīh ysūg (خليه يسوق)
to a woman: khallīhum yiyūn (خليهم ييون)
make sure Fahad knows (to a man)
to a woman: khallī Fahad yaʿarf; just to pass on news, say khabbir Fahad (خبر فهد); khalli + any name + verb: khalli Sēf ysūg = let Sēf drive
he wants to come: yabi yiyi (يبي ييي)
there's no room in it (a car, a room)
in it (m.): ma fīh makān (ما فيه مكان)
do you want to come with us? (to a man)
to a woman: tabīn tiyīn wiyyāna? (تبين تيين ويانا؟)
we'll all go, let's all go
see you on Saturday (to a man)
to a woman: nshūfich is-sabt (نشوفج السبت)

title: Don't make me go on my own
goal: Sēf wants to skip the cinema tonight; talk him round without keeping him out late
tip: la tkhallīni + a verb with a- means 'don't make me' or 'don't let me': la tkhallīni arūḥ b-rūḥi 'don't make me go on my own'. On its own, la tkhallīni is 'don't leave me'. About someone else: ykhallīni atrayya 'he keeps me waiting'. To a woman it's the same: la tkhallīni; to a group: la tkhallūni.
grammar: la tkhallīni + verb: 'don't make me / don't leave me'
dialogue: A
سامحني، ما أقدر أيي السينما الليلة. المفروض أدرس
sāmiḥni, ma agdar ayi s-sīnama l-lēla. il-mafrūẓ adris
Sorry, I can't make the cinema tonight. I'm supposed to be studying.
B
لا عاد! لا تخليني أروح بروحي
la ʿād! la tkhallīni arūḥ b-rūḥi
Oh, come on! Don't make me go on my own.
A
عيل فهد؟ خله يروح وياك، هو فاضي الليلة
ʿayal Fahad? khallah yrūḥ wiyyāk, huwa fāẓi l-lēla
What about Fahad, then? Let him go with you; he's free tonight.
B
فهد؟ لا! كل مرة يتأخر ويخليني أتريا ساعة
Fahad? la! kill marra yitʼakhkhar w ykhallīni atrayya sāʿa
Fahad? No way! He's late every time and keeps me waiting an hour.
A
صح والله. زين، الفلم الساعة كم؟
ṣaḥḥ wallāh. zēn, il-film is-sāʿa cham?
That's true. OK, what time's the film?
B
تسع. ادرس العصر، ومب لازم تيي بدري
tisʿ. idris il-ʿaṣir, w mub lāzim tiyi badri
Nine. Study this afternoon; you don't need to come early.
A
زين، بس لا تخليني أتأخر. لازم أنام بدري
zēn, bas la tkhallīni atʼakhkhar. lāzim anām badri
OK, but don't keep me out late. I need to get to bed early.
B
لا تخاف! بعد الفلم، نرجع على طول
la tkhāf! baʿd il-film, nirjaʿ ʿala ṭūl
Don't worry! Straight after the film, we'll head back.
items: don't make me, don't leave me (to a man)
to a woman: the same, la tkhallīni (لا تخليني); to a group: la tkhallūni (لا تخلوني)
don't make me go on my own (to a man)
to a woman: the same, la tkhallīni arūḥ b-rūḥi
he keeps me waiting, he makes me wait
she keeps me waiting: tkhallīni atrayya (تخليني أتريا)
don't make me late, don't keep me out late (to a man)
to a woman: the same, la tkhallīni atʼakhkhar
I can't come, I can't make it
ma agdar ayi l-lēla = I can't make it tonight
I need to get to bed early, I have to sleep early
she's late every time: kill marra titʼakhkhar (كل مرة تتأخر)
we'll come straight back, we'll head straight home

title: Let him sleep, guys
goal: At Sēf's place, Fahad wants to wake Sēf up so the guys can go out; tell them all to let him sleep
tip: To a group, khalli becomes khallū-: khallūh ynām 'let him sleep', khallūha 'leave it (f.)', khallūhum 'leave them'. Before -lah 'for him' the u stays long: khallū-lah warga 'leave him a note'. Other group commands end in -u too: rūḥu intu 'you go'.
dialogue: A
سيف نايم! شنو رأيك، نصحيه؟
Sēf nāyim! shinu raʼyak, nṣaḥḥīh?
Sēf's asleep! What do you reckon, shall we wake him up?
B
لا يا شباب، خلوه ينام. توه خلص امتحانه
la yā shabāb, khallūh ynām. tawwah khallaṣ imtiḥānah
No, guys, let him sleep. He's only just finished his exam.
A
بس إحنا المفروض نطلع الحين، وهو قال: صحوني!
bas iḥna l-mafrūẓ niṭlaʿ il-ḥīn, w huwa gāl: ṣaḥḥūni!
But we're supposed to head out now, and he said, "Wake me up!"
B
خلوه على راحته. مب لازم يطلع وياكم
khallūh ʿala rāḥtah. mub lāzim yiṭlaʿ wiyyākum
Leave him be. He doesn't have to come out with you.
A
زين، وإذا صحى وما لقانا؟
zēn, w idha ṣiḥa w ma ligāna?
OK, and if he wakes up and can't find us?
B
خلوا له ورقة على الطاولة
khallū-lah warga ʿala ṭ-ṭāwla
Leave him a note on the table.
A
فكرة حلوة. وانت؟ تبي تيي ويانا؟
fikra ḥilwa. w inta? tabi tiyi wiyyāna?
Good idea. And you? Do you want to come with us?
B
لا، روحوا انتو. أنا بقعد وياه شوي
la, rūḥu intu. ana bagʿid wiyyāh shwayy
No, you lot go. I'll stay with him for a bit.
items: leave him, let him be (to a group)
to one man: khallah (خله); to one woman: khallīh (خليه); same spelling, past: khallōh 'they left him'
to one man: khallah ynām (خله ينام); to one woman: khallīh ynām (خليه ينام)
leave him be, let him do as he likes (to a group)
to one man: khallah ʿala rāḥtah (خله على راحته); to one woman: khallīh ʿala rāḥtah
leave him a note (to a group)
to one man or one woman: khallī-lah warga (خلي له ورقة); leave me a note: khallū-li warga (خلوا لي ورقة)
she's only just finished: tawwha khallaṣat (توها خلصت)
if he wakes up, when he wakes up
if she wakes up: idha ṣiḥat (إذا صحت)
to one man: ṣaḥḥni (صحني); to one woman: ṣaḥḥīni (صحيني)
you go (on), you lot go (to a group)
to one man: rūḥ inta (روح انت); to one woman: rūḥi inti (روحي انتي)

title: Leave it to me
goal: As you leave the office, Maryam is still at her desk with a report; offer to help, suggest finishing it tomorrow and deal with the manager
tip: To a woman, khalli becomes khallī-: khallīni asāʿdich 'let me help you', khallīh ʿalay 'leave it (him) to me'. khallīna + a we-verb is 'let's': khallīna nkhalliṣ. No word for 'to' comes between khalli and the verb.
grammar: khallī- + object + verb (to a woman); khallīna 'let's' (recycle)
dialogue: B
مريم، للحين هني؟ الساعة سبع!
Maryam, lil-ḥīn hni? is-sāʿa sabʿ!
Maryam, still here? It's seven o'clock!
A
هيه، التقرير ما خلص، والمدير يبيه الصبح
hē, it-taqrīr ma khilaṣ, w il-mudīr yabīh iṣ-ṣubḥ
Yes, the report isn't finished, and the manager wants it in the morning.
B
خليني أساعدج. عطيني الأرقام
khallīni asāʿdich. ʿaṭīni l-argām
Let me help you. Give me the figures.
A
لا، مشكور. بس الأرقام يبالها وقت وايد
la, mashkūr. bas il-argām yabā-lha wagt wāyid
No, thanks. It's just that the figures will take ages.
B
عيل خلينا نخلص التقرير باكر قبل الدوام، ويا بعض
ʿayal khallīna nkhalliṣ it-taqrīr bāchir gabil id-dawām, wiyya baʿaẓ
Then let's finish the report together tomorrow, before work.
A
زين. والمدير؟ ما أبيه يزعل
zēn. w il-mudīr? ma abīh yizʿal
OK. And the manager? I don't want him to be annoyed.
B
خليه علي، أنا بكلمه. يعطيج العافية!
khallīh ʿalay, ana bakallmah. yaʿṭīch il-ʿāfya!
Leave him to me, I'll talk to him. Thanks for all your hard work!
A
الله يعافيك. نشوفك باكر إن شاء الله
allāh yʿāfīk. nshūfak bāchir in shāʼ allāh
Thank you. See you tomorrow, God willing.
items: let me help you (to a woman)
to a man: khallni asāʿdak (خلني أساعدك)
leave it to me, leave him to me (to a woman)
to a man: khallah ʿalay (خله علي); a feminine thing: khallīha ʿalay (خليها علي); don't confuse it with khallha ʿalay (خلها علي, to a man) 'it's on me, I'll pay'
the report isn't finished, the report isn't done
khilaṣ = it's finished, it's over; khallaṣt = I finished (it)
also: baʿdak hni? (بعدك هني؟) to a man, baʿdich hni? (بعدج هني؟) to a woman
I don't want him to get upset, I don't want him annoyed
about a woman: ma abīha tizʿal (ما أبيها تزعل)
we finish the report; shall we finish the report?
the figures will take time, the numbers need time
give me the figures (to a woman)
to a man: ʿaṭni l-argām (عطني الأرقام); to a group: ʿaṭūni l-argām (عطوني الأرقام)

title: We never see you any more!
goal: Back from a month in London, visit Bū Rāshid's majlis, apologise for staying away and catch up
tip: ma ʿād + a present verb means 'not any more': ma ʿād amshi wāyid 'I don't walk much any more'. ʿād can also take the person: ma ʿidt atḥammal il-bard 'I can't take the cold any more', ma ʿidna nshūfak 'we never see you any more'.
grammar: ma ʿād / ma ʿidt + verb: 'not any more'
dialogue: A
هلا والله! وينك يا ولدي؟ ما عدنا نشوفك!
hala wallāh! wēnak yā wildi? ma ʿidna nshūfak!
Well, hello! Where've you been, son? We never see you any more!
B
هلا بك يا عمي! سامحني، كنت في لندن شهر
hala bik yā ʿammi! sāmiḥni, kint fi Landan shahar
Hello, uncle! Forgive me, I was in London for a month.
A
الحمد لله على السلامة. ولندن؟ باردة؟
il-ḥamdu lillāh ʿala s-salāma. w Landan? bārda?
Welcome back. And London? Was it cold?
B
الله يسلمك. باردة وايد! ما عدت أتحمل البرد
allāh ysallmak. bārda wāyid! ma ʿidt atḥammal il-bard
Thank you. Very cold! I can't take the cold any more.
A
صرت مثلنا يا ولدي! وأنا ما عاد أمشي وايد، ريولي تعورني
ṣirt mithilna yā wildi! w ana ma ʿād amshi wāyid, ryūli tʿawwirni
You've become like us, son! As for me, I don't walk much any more; my legs hurt.
B
سلامات يا عمي!
salāmāt yā ʿammi!
Oh dear, get well soon, uncle!
A
الله يسلمك. بس انت لا تغيب عنا مرة ثانية!
allāh ysallmak. bas inta la tghīb ʿanna marra thānya!
Thank you. But don't you stay away from us again!
B
إن شاء الله يا عمي. المفروض أييكم كل أسبوع
in shāʼ allāh yā ʿammi. il-mafrūẓ ayīkum kill usbūʿ
I won't, God willing, uncle. I ought to come and see you every week.
items: not any more, no longer (before a verb)
ma ʿād amshi wāyid = I don't walk much any more; Kuwait: the same
we never see you any more, you've disappeared (to a man)
to a woman: ma ʿidna nshūfich (ما عدنا نشوفج); ʿād takes the person: ma ʿidt 'I no longer', ma ʿidna 'we no longer'
I no longer, I'm not … any more; you no longer (to a man)
to a woman: ma ʿidti (ما عدتي); ma ʿād works for 'I' too: ma ʿād agdar = I can't any more
I can't take the cold any more
atḥammal = I bear, I put up with
I don't walk much any more
my legs hurt, my feet hurt
my head hurts: rāsi yʿawwirni (راسي يعورني)
don't stay away from us, don't be a stranger (to a man)
to a woman: la tghībīn ʿanna (لا تغيبين عنا)
I come to you (all), I come and see you (all)
to one man: ayīk (أييك); I'll come and see you: bayīkum (بييكم)
I was in London for a month
kint = I was, you were (to a man)
culture: When an elder hasn't seen you for a while, expect a warm welcome with a friendly complaint: hala wallāh! wēnak? ma ʿidna nshūfak! Answer the welcome (hala bik), apologise for staying away (sāmiḥni) and say where you were. Someone back from a trip is welcomed with il-ḥamdu lillāh ʿala s-salāma (reply: allāh ysallmak). If he says he's unwell, answer with salāmāt.

title: Are you still asleep?
goal: On a Saturday morning, ring Sēf, find out who's still away and plan lunch
tip: baʿad + an ending means 'still': baʿadni 'I'm still', baʿdak 'you're still', baʿdah 'he's still'. Add a place, a participle or ma + past: baʿdak nāyim? 'are you still asleep?', baʿdah ma yā 'he still hasn't come'. lil-ḥīn means the same.
dialogue: B
هلا سيف! بعدك نايم؟ الساعة عشر!
hala Sēf! baʿdak nāyim? is-sāʿa ʿashr!
Hi Sēf! Are you still asleep? It's ten o'clock!
A
هلا فيك! لا، صاحي. بس بعدني على السرير
hala fīk! la, ṣāḥi. bas baʿadni ʿala s-sirīr
Hi! No, I'm awake. But I'm still in bed.
B
يلا قوم! ودي أشوفك، ما شفتك من شهر
yalla gūm! widdi ashūfak, ma shiftak min shahar
Come on, get up! I want to see you; I haven't seen you for a month.
A
صح والله! بعدك تعبان من السفر؟
ṣaḥḥ wallāh! baʿdak taʿbān min is-safar?
That's true! Are you still tired from the trip?
B
شوي. وفهد؟ بعده في الكويت؟
shwayy. w Fahad? baʿdah fi l-Kwēt?
A bit. And Fahad? Is he still in Kuwait?
A
هيه، بعده ما يا. ما عاد يبي يرجع!
hē, baʿdah ma yā. ma ʿād yabi yirjaʿ!
Yes, he still hasn't come back. He doesn't want to come back any more!
B
زين. عيل نتغدى اليوم؟ لا تخليني آكل بروحي!
zēn. ʿayal nitghadda l-yōm? la tkhallīni ākil b-rūḥi!
OK. Then shall we have lunch today? Don't make me eat on my own!
A
ماشي. بس عطني ساعة، بعدني ما تريقت!
māshi. bas ʿaṭni sāʿa, baʿadni ma trayyagt!
Sure. But give me an hour; I haven't even had breakfast yet!
items: are you still asleep? (to a man)
to a woman: baʿdich nāyma? (بعدج نايمة؟)
baʿadni ʿala s-sirīr = I'm still in bed; lil-ḥīn (للحين) means the same
he still hasn't come, he isn't here yet
baʿdah fi = he's still in (a place)
are you still tired? (to a man)
to a woman: baʿdich taʿbāna? (بعدج تعبانة؟)
give me an hour (to a man)
to a woman: ʿaṭīni sāʿa (عطيني ساعة)
he doesn't want to come back any more
about a woman: ma ʿād tabi tirjaʿ (ما عاد تبي ترجع)
culture: Since January 2022 the UAE's official weekend has been Saturday and Sunday, with a short working day on Friday for government staff; before that it was Friday and Saturday. So a lazy Saturday morning is normal.

title: How many have you got left?
goal: Catch up with Sēf on his exams, ask what's left and plan a desert trip for when they're over
tip: bāgi means 'left, remaining'. bāgi-li + a noun: 'I've got … left' (bāgi-li imtiḥānēn). bāgi ʿala + an event: how long until it (bāgi ʿala l-ijāza usbūʿ 'a week to go till the holidays'). ma bāgi shay 'there's nothing left'; cham bāgi? 'how long to go?'
dialogue: B
سيف! بعدك تدرس؟ باقي لك وايد؟
Sēf! baʿdak tidris? bāgi-lak wāyid?
Sēf! Still studying? Have you got many left?
A
لا، باقي لي امتحانين بس، الحمد لله
la, bāgi-li imtiḥānēn bas, il-ḥamdu lillāh
No, I've only got two exams left, thank God.
B
زين! ومتى آخر امتحان؟
zēn! w mita ākhir imtiḥān?
Great! And when's the last exam?
A
يوم الخميس، وبعدين الإجازة!
yōm il-khamīs, w baʿdēn il-ijāza!
On Thursday, and then it's the holidays!
B
وأنا خلصت المشروع في الشغل. ما باقي شي!
w ana khallaṣt il-mashrūʿ fi sh-shughul. ma bāgi shay!
And I've finished the project at work. There's nothing left!
A
ما شاء الله! عيل بعد الامتحانات نروح كلنا البر
mā shāʼ allāh! ʿayal baʿd il-imtiḥānāt nrūḥ killna l-barr
Great stuff! Then after the exams we'll all go to the desert.
B
أكيد! وخبر فهد. كم باقي على الإجازة؟
akīd! w khabbir Fahad. cham bāgi ʿala l-ijāza?
Definitely! And let Fahad know. How long till the holidays?
A
ثلاث أيام بس. يلا، خلني أدرس الحين!
thalāth ayyām bas. yalla, khallni adris il-ḥīn!
Just three days. Right, let me get on with studying!
items: have you got much left? have you got many left? (to a man)
to a woman: bāgi-lich wāyid? (باقي لج وايد؟)
I've got … left, I still have
bāgi-li imtiḥānēn = I've got two exams left
bāgi ʿala l-ijāza usbūʿ = a week to go till the holidays
how long till …? how long to go?
cham bāgi? = how much is left? how long to go?
let me study, let me get on with studying (to a man)
to a woman: khallīni adris (خليني أدرس)

title: I kept ringing you!
goal: Fahad is back from Kuwait; find out why he didn't answer and what he did with his family
tip: tamm + a present verb means 'kept on doing': tammēt adigg ʿalēk 'I kept ringing you', tamm yisʼal 'he kept asking'. On its own it means 'stayed'. tammēt is 'I' or 'you (to a man)', tammēna 'we'. Fahad, a Kuwaiti, says ẓall: ẓallēt, ẓall ygūl.
grammar: tamm + present verb: 'kept on'; tammēt 'I stayed' (also ẓall)
dialogue: B
وينك يا فهد؟ تميت أدق عليك يومين!
wēnak yā Fahad? tammēt adigg ʿalēk yōmēn!
Where've you been, Fahad? I kept ringing you for two days!
A
آسف، كنت في الكويت وتلفوني خرب. توني راجع!
āsif, kint fi l-Kwēt w tilifōni khirab. tawwni rājiʿ!
Sorry, I was in Kuwait and my phone broke. I've only just got back!
B
الحمد لله على السلامة! سيف تم يسأل عنك. شو سويت هناك؟
il-ḥamdu lillāh ʿala s-salāma! Sēf tamm yisʼal ʿannak. shu sawwēt hnāk?
Welcome back! Sēf kept asking about you. What did you get up to there?
A
الله يسلمك. ظليت ويا أهلي، وأمي ظلت تطبخ كل يوم!
allāh ysallmak. ẓallēt wiyya ahli, w ummi ẓallat tiṭbakh kill yōm!
Thanks. I stayed with my family, and my mum kept cooking every day!
B
حلو! أكيد تميت تاكل طول اليوم
ḥilu! akīd tammēt tākil ṭūl il-yōm
Nice! I bet you kept eating all day.
A
إيه والله! وأبوي ظل يقول: كل بعد!
ēh wallāh! w ubūy ẓall ygūl: kil baʿad!
Yeah, honestly! And my dad kept saying, "Have some more!"
B
عيل ما عاد تبي غدا اليوم؟
ʿayal ma ʿād tabi ghada l-yōm?
So you don't want lunch any more today?
A
لا لا، أبي! بس خلنا ناكل شي خفيف
la la, abi! bas khallna nākil shay khafīf
No, no, I do! But let's have something light.

to a woman: tammēti (تميتي); also: ẓallēt (ظليت), more common in Kuwait
I kept ringing you, I kept calling you (to a man)
to a woman: tammēt adigg ʿalēch (تميت أدق عليج); also: ẓallēt adigg (ظليت أدق), more common in Kuwait
he kept asking about you (to a man)
to a woman: tamm yisʼal ʿannich (تم يسأل عنج); also: ẓall (ظل), more common in Kuwait
to a woman: tammēti tāklīn (تميتي تاكلين); I kept eating: tammēt ākil
she cooks every day; you cook every day (to a man)
to a woman: tiṭbakhīn kill yōm (تطبخين كل يوم)
my phone broke, my phone's broken
a feminine thing: is-sayyāra khirbat = the car broke down

have some more, eat some more (to a man)
to a woman: kili baʿad (كلي بعد)
culture: Gulf hosts, and Gulf mums, keep pressing food on you: 'kil baʿad!' again and again. It shows generosity. To stop politely, say la wallāh, shbaʿt, il-ḥamdu lillāh once or twice.

title: Checkpoint 3.4: working late
goal: Checkpoint: Maryam and a colleague are still at the office; offer to help them finish the presentation
tip: Group and 'we' forms of this block: baʿadkum 'you're still (all of you)', bāgi-lna 'we've got … left', tammēna 'we kept on', la tkhallūni 'don't make me (to a group)'. ma ʿād fīni means 'I've had enough, I'm worn out'.
grammar: checkpoint 3.4: recycle s3u052–s3u064 (obligation, khalli, still / no longer / left)
dialogue: B
انتو بعدكم هني؟ الساعة ثمان!
intu baʿadkum hni? is-sāʿa thamān!
Are you still here? It's eight o'clock!
A
هيه، العرض يباله شغل، وباقي لنا ساعة بس
hē, il-ʿarẓ yabā-lah shughul, w bāgi-lna sāʿa bas
Yes, the presentation needs work, and we've only got an hour left.
B
عيل خلوني أساعدكم. شو باقي؟
ʿayal khallūni asāʿidkum. shu bāgi?
Then let me help you. What's left?
A
الأرقام بس. تمينا نشتغل عليها طول العصر، ما عاد فيني
il-argām bas. tammēna nishtaghil ʿalēha ṭūl il-ʿaṣir, ma ʿād fīni
Just the figures. We've been at them all afternoon; I'm worn out.
B
عطوني الملف، أنا أخلصها. مب لازم تقعدون، روحوا انتو البيت
ʿaṭūni l-malaff, ana akhalliṣha. mub lāzim tigʿdūn, rūḥu intu l-bēt
Give me the file, I'll finish them. You don't need to stay; you two go home.
A
لا والله، ما نخليك بروحك! نخلصها ويا بعض
la wallāh, ma nkhallīk b-rūḥak! nkhalliṣha wiyya baʿaẓ
No way, we won't leave you on your own! We'll finish them together.
B
زين، بس لا تخلوني أكتب الإيميل حق المدير! ما عدت أقدر
zēn, bas la tkhallūni aktib il-īmēl ḥagg il-mudīr! ma ʿidt agdar
OK, but don't make me write the email to the manager! I can't do any more.
A
لا تخاف، الإيميل علي!
la tkhāf, il-īmēl ʿalay!
Don't worry, leave the email to me!
